'''History of Star Wars CCG formats''' traces what "format" and "constructed" meant over the life of the game: how [[Decipher]] described its tournaments from 1996 to 2001, how the [[Players Committee]] named its card pools after 2002, and why this wiki gives each historical card pool its own name. The list of formats themselves is on [[Formats]].

== Decipher: one game, growing pool (1995–2001) ==

=== "Any and all cards" ===
Decipher's first organizer's guide, released in August 1996, set no card pool at all: "Any and all cards from the Star Wars™ Customizable Card Game™ universe are allowed in play at tournaments." A standard tournament deck was 60 cards, with no limit on copies of a card.<ref name="tg96">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/tournamentguide.pdf Organizer's Guide: Tournament Rules System, August 1996 Release] (PDF), Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219040510/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/tournamentguide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> The rule held for the rest of Decipher's run. Its 1999 guide said: "In sanctioned tournaments, of any format, there are no restrictions on any particular cards in the game", and cards were "allowable for use in tournaments as soon as they are released".<ref name="tg9905">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/swtournamentguide/formats.html Tournament Guide: II. Formats], Decipher (May 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990502214324/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/swtournamentguide/formats.html Internet Archive].</ref> By 2001 the only exception was a one-week delay before new cards were legal at Championship Circuit events.<ref name="legal01">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/releasedatesandlegality.asp Release Dates and Tournament Legality], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011116132908/http://tournaments.decipher.com/releasedatesandlegality.asp Internet Archive].</ref>

So in Decipher's eyes there was one constructed game, and each new expansion simply joined it. Decipher had no name for "the cards legal in July 1999"; a player in 1999 and a player in 2001 were both just playing Star Wars CCG.

=== What Decipher called a format ===
For Decipher, a ''format'' was a kind of tournament, not a card pool. Its names for the standard two-deck Swiss event changed over the years:<ref name="tg96" /><ref name="ov98">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html Tournaments overview], Decipher (1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717031138/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="tg9905" /><ref name="tg9906">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/pdfs/tournamentguide0699.pdf Decipher Customizable Card Group Tournament Guide] ("TD GUIDE 6.99", PDF), Decipher (June 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903022456/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/pdfs/tournamentguide0699.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="ch01">[http://decipher.com/tournaments/changes2001/index.html Additions to the 2001 Sanctioned Tournament Program], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010203173600/http://decipher.com/tournaments/changes2001/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

{| class="wikitable"
! Year !! Decipher's name for constructed play !! Other sanctioned formats

The June 1999 guide, rewritten to cover all of Decipher's card games, put it plainly: "Decipher sanctions three basic formats: Constructed Deck, Junior, and Sealed Deck." Constructed Deck meant each player came "with decks already constructed according to the standard rules for that game".<ref name="tg9906" /><ref name="tgtypes">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentguide/tournamenttypesandformats.html Official Tournament Guide: II. Tournament Types and Formats], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000109144553/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/tournamentguide/tournamenttypesandformats.html Internet Archive].</ref> Each format had its own player rating.<ref name="tg9905" />

=== Sealed deck and the "enhanced format" ===
Sealed deck began as an unsanctioned beginner's event: "By simply bringing one sealed starter deck to a tournament everyone will be playing with the 'fate' of the cards."<ref name="tg96" /> By 1998 it was sanctioned, and Decipher made the [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] product for it, designating every event run with it as the "enhanced format".<ref name="otsd98">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/sealeddeck.htm Using the Official Tournament Sealed Deck], Decipher (1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980506110410/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/sealeddeck.htm Internet Archive].</ref> Product-based variants followed: [[OTSD Booster Draft]], [[EPP Overdrive]] (1999), [[Endor Draft]] (1999) and [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck (format)|Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] (2000). Unlike constructed play, these formats were fixed: the product defined the pool. See [[Sealed Deck]] and [[Enhanced Format Sealed Deck]].

=== Closed environments (2000–2001) ===
The first time Decipher limited the constructed card pool was in 2000. It launched "three new sanctioned Tournament Formats" built from the [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] and [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] cards, then renamed them: "In order to place the focus where it belongs - on the dynamic new Death Star II cards - the formats are renamed 'Death Star II Closed Environment.'"<ref name="ds2ren">[http://www2.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/deathstar2/index.html Death Star II Closed Environment], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001211203400/http://www2.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/deathstar2/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> The [[Death Star II Closed Environment]] covered constructed, booster draft and sealed play. In August 2001 the [[Episode I Closed Environment]] followed: "a format where players build decks using only cards that have an Episode I icon".<ref name="ep1">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/episodei.html Episode I Closed Environment Tournament Format], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011004151018/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/episodei.html Internet Archive].</ref> From 1 January 2001 Decipher kept a separate Closed Environment rating, and its 2001 program called the normal game the "Standard Constructed Deck" format to tell the two apart.<ref name="ch01" /> Players also spoke of the Episode I environment as "Type II"<ref name="dt18697">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18697 Dredlox's Type II HardCore Senators], Neal Razi, DeckTech (31 August 2001): "a type II(Ep 1) dedicated Senate Deck". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017024622/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18697/ Internet Archive].</ref> (see [[Episode I Closed Environment]]); no Decipher page found uses that term.

At conventions Decipher ran one-off variants such as [[Highlander]], [[Kibitzing]], [[Race for Alderaan Constructed]] and [[Turning of a Skywalker Constructed]] at [[DecipherCon 2000]], and [[Iron Man]] and [[No Such Thing As Luck]] at [[DecipherCon 1999]].

=== "Open" ===
In Decipher's material "Open" described who could play, not which cards: the 1999 "Wild Card" Open Championship, the 2001 "World Championship Open Qualifiers" ("Any player may play in these events"), and the 2002 Territorial Open, Open and Mini-Open championships.<ref name="dc99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events.html DecipherCon 1999 events], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122042301/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="circ01">[http://www.decipher.com/tournaments/circuit2001/index.html Championship Circuit 2001], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010318003744/http://www.decipher.com/tournaments/circuit2001/index.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="cc02">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/champcircuit/index.html 2002 Championship Circuit], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020810221521/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/champcircuit/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> No Decipher page found uses "Open" as the name of a card pool.

== Players Committee (2002–) ==
From March 2002 the Players Committee added its own Virtual Sets to the Decipher pool, and championship constructed again meant "everything legal on the day", now including the latest virtual cards (see [[Virtual Original]]). In July 2014 the PC reset the virtual pool and named two constructed formats: '''Standard''' (post-reset virtual cards) and '''Legacy''' (the earlier ones).<ref name="reset">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/reset-of-standard-format/ Reset of Standard Format], Advocate Council (byline darkjediknight11), Players Committee (25 July 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170306155342/http://www.starwarsccg.org/reset-of-standard-format/ Internet Archive, 6 March 2017]</ref> The PC's 2015 Alternate Format Tournament Guide and its 2019 formats page use those names, while the [[GEMP]] client calls the current pool '''[[Open]]''', and PC articles used "Open" by December 2020.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Like Decipher, the PC names the current pool rather than each period's: "Standard" or "Open" in 2016 and in 2026 are both just the latest cards, although the virtual sets and errata in between changed the game.

== How this wiki names historical card pools ==
Because neither Decipher nor the Players Committee named the card pool of a given period, this wiki does, after the last set it contains: [[Premiere - Endor]] is every Decipher card legal from June 1999 (the [[1999 Decipher World Championship]] pool), [[Premiere - Death Star II]] the [[2000 Decipher World Championship]] pool, and [[Premiere - Original VS3]] the pool of the [[2002 World Championship]]. The names describe what was actually legal, which is what a player needs to rebuild or replay a deck of the time. Formats whose definition never changed, such as a sealed product or a closed environment, keep their originator's own name, with other names noted on their pages. Many of these period names are also [[GEMP]] formats, where retro events are played today.
